column1: OWASP API Top 10 (2023) | NIST SP 800-204 | CWE/SANS Top 25 | PCI-DSS v4.0 | ISO/IEC 27001:2022
STATUS:  Passed = compliant  |  Failed = remediation required  |  Partial = partially met  |  Pending = not yet tested  |  N/A = not applicable

column2: Control / Test Description
Ensure every API request is authenticated — no anonymous access to protected endpoints.
Enforce strong authentication: Basic Auth only over HTTPS, OAuth 2.0, or JWT. Confirm correct implementation of each.
Implement MFA where risk warrants it (e.g., certificate-based second factor, TOTP, FIDO2/WebAuthn).
Anti-brute-force controls on auth endpoints: account lockout, progressive delays, CAPTCHA, rate-limiting.
Passwords must be salted and hashed with bcrypt/scrypt/Argon2 (min cost factor 10). No MD5/SHA-1.
JWT: use complex secret (≥256-bit), enforce algorithm server-side (HS256/RS256 — no 'alg:none'), set short TTL, never store sensitive data in payload.
OAuth 2.0: validate redirect_uri server-side (whitelist only); use PKCE for public clients; use 'code' flow not implicit; enforce state param against CSRF; scope validation per client.
No credentials, auth tokens, or passwords in URL query strings or HTTP GET parameters.
API Keys: enforce rotation policy, never embed in client-side code, transmit only via headers (X-API-Key), associate to IP/service allowlist.
Session tokens must be invalidated server-side on logout and expiry.
Implement role-based or attribute-based access control (RBAC/ABAC); enforce user hierarchy on every endpoint.
Broken Object-Level Authorization (BOLA/IDOR): verify logged-in user can only access their own records.
Use non-guessable identifiers (UUID v4) for all resource IDs - no sequential integers.
Enforce correct HTTP verbs; reject mis-matched method/resource combinations (405 Method Not Allowed).
Broken Function-Level Authorization (BFLA): admin-only functions must not be reachable by standard users.
Mass Assignment: API must not accept and apply unintended fields (e.g., 'role','isAdmin') from client payload.
Ensure cross-tenant isolation in multi-tenant environments — no data bleed between tenants.
API responses must return only fields needed by the consumer — no over-fetching of sensitive fields.
Tokens, bearer tokens, PINs, and passwords must never appear in logs in plaintext.
Disable verbose/stack-trace error messages in production; return generic error with correlation ID only.
Sensitive parameters (passwords, PINs, card numbers) encrypted in transit AND at rest.
All API endpoints served exclusively over HTTPS (no HTTP fallback); HSTS header enforced.
TLS 1.2 minimum (TLS 1.3 preferred); disable SSLv3, TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1; only strong cipher suites.
No sensitive data in HTTP headers sent to client (e.g., internal IPs, debug headers, session tokens in Location).
PII masking: partial masking applied to card numbers, national IDs, and account numbers in API responses.
Implement rate limiting per client/IP/token; return 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After header.
Enforce max payload size on all input fields (string length, array element count, file size).
Implement query complexity/depth limits for GraphQL or nested REST resources.
Protect file upload endpoints: validate MIME type, enforce max file size, scan for malware.
Apply geo/IP-based throttling or blocking on high-risk endpoints (e.g., OTP, login, payment).
Send X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff on all responses.
Send X-Frame-Options: DENY (or CSP frame-ancestors 'none') to prevent clickjacking.
Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none' — restrict resource loading.
Remove server fingerprinting headers (X-Powered-By, Server, X-AspNet-Version, X-Generator).
Enforce response Content-Type strictly matching actual content (e.g., application/json).
Never return credentials, passwords, or security tokens in response bodies.
Return correct HTTP status codes for every operation type (200, 201, 400, 401, 403, 404, 405, 429, 500).
CORS policy: restrict Access-Control-Allow-Origin to known domains; no wildcard (*) on credentialed requests.
Disable debug mode, admin consoles (Swagger UI, GraphiQL), and test endpoints in production.
API versioning enforced; deprecated versions return 410 Gone after sunset date.
All input validation via single, centralised, actively maintained library (no ad-hoc validation).
Validate, filter, and sanitise all client-supplied and third-party integration data.
Escape special characters using context-appropriate encoding for target interpreter (HTML, SQL, LDAP, OS).
Use parameterised queries / ORM — never concatenate user input into SQL/NoSQL queries.
Limit records returned per query to prevent mass data disclosure via injection.
Accept-list validation: only allow explicitly permitted values per input parameter.
Define strict data types and regex patterns for all string parameters (format enforcement).
XML/JSON bomb and XXE prevention: reject deeply nested structures; disable external entity processing.
Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) prevention: validate and allowlist URL inputs; block internal IP ranges.
Command/LDAP/XPath injection: sanitise all fields used in system calls, directory queries, XML path expressions.
Log all failed authentication attempts, access denials, input validation errors, and rate-limit triggers.
Log all inbound requests and outbound responses (excluding sensitive payloads).
Logs formatted in structured JSON consumable by SIEM (Kibana).
Log contains actual client source IP (not load-balancer IP); use X-Forwarded-For with validation.
Raw HTTP access logs AND transactional logs shipped to centralised log aggregation platform.
Immutable audit trail for all financial/payment transactions: record who, what, when, from where.
Log retention policy enforced: As per NCBA Policy
Alerting rules configured for anomalous patterns: spike in 401/403 responses, unusual transaction volume, after-hours admin access.
Maintain a complete, up-to-date API inventory (OpenAPI/Swagger spec) for all internal and external APIs.
Deprecated API endpoints return 410 Gone; no legacy endpoints process live transactions.
